# Pipeline Stories
# Generated by agent-story-writer from docs/architecture-recap.md

---
EPIC: Infrastructure
STORY-1: Shared enriched customer data models

As a developer
I want shared C# record models for the enriched customer document
So that both function apps have a consistent, typed representation of the Cosmos DB document

Acceptance criteria:
- Given the project is compiled
  When EnrichedCustomer is instantiated
  Then it must expose PartyId, SchemaVersion, LastUpdatedAt, LastUpdatedBy, Version, Customer, Addresses, PhoneNumbers, EmailAddresses, BankOperations, Onboarding, and AuditSummary properties
- Given an Address record is created with an invalid AddressType
  When the code is compiled
  Then it fails to compile (enum enforced at compile time — no runtime casting)
- Given a TaxInfo record is created
  When TaxId is stored
  Then only the last 4 digits are held (masking is applied by the onboarding hydration step before assembly — not enforced by the model itself)
- Given a collection property (Addresses, PhoneNumbers, EmailAddresses, BankOperations) is not explicitly set
  When the EnrichedCustomer is instantiated
  Then the property defaults to an empty list rather than null

Technical notes:
- Use `record` types with `init`-only properties throughout (immutable DTOs)
- `EnrichedCustomer`: `Id` (string) and `PartyId` (string) hold the same value — `partyId` is both the Cosmos `id` and partition key
- Collection defaults: `List<Address> Addresses { get; init; } = [];` (same pattern for all four collections)
- `TaxInfo`: `TaxIdType` enum (`SSN`, `EIN`) discriminates the two mutually exclusive tax ID types; `TaxId` stores masked value only
- Enums to define: `TaxIdType { SSN, EIN }`, `AddressType { Primary, Secondary, Mailing, Billing, Previous }`, `PhoneType { Mobile, Home, Work, Fax }`, `EmailType { Personal, Work, Other }`
- Every collection item carries `AddedAt` (DateTimeOffset) and `AddedBy` (string) for per-item audit
- Stable IDs on every collection item: `AddressId`, `PhoneId`, `EmailId`, `OperationId` — used as single-field lookup keys by the amendment app
- `IsPreferred` bool on `Address`, `PhoneNumber`, and `EmailAddress` — exactly one preferred per collection; enforcement is the amendment validator's responsibility, not the model
- `AuditSummary` nested record: `LastMessageId`, `LastKafkaOffset` (long), `LastHydrationSteps` (List<string>), `WasApiFallback` (bool), `ProcessedAt` (DateTimeOffset)
- `OnboardingInfo` nested record: `CompletedAt` (DateTimeOffset), `ExternalCustomerNo` (string), `EffectiveDate` (string)
- Use `sealed` on all concrete record types not designed for inheritance
- Phone numbers stored in E.164 format — no runtime format validation in the model

EPIC: Infrastructure
STORY-2: Kafka message and pipeline context models

As a developer
I want shared C# record models for Kafka metadata, pipeline state, hydration results, and audit documents
So that both function apps share a single, typed definition for every message-lifecycle object

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a KafkaMessageContext is created with all properties
  When it is passed downstream
  Then MessageId, PartyId, Topic, Partition, Offset, TopicRole, and ReceivedAt are all accessible and immutable
- Given a HydrationContext is passed to an IEnrichmentStep
  When the step attempts to mutate a property
  Then it fails to compile (init-only record properties)
- Given an AuditRecord is created for a successful processing run
  When ToCosmosDocument is called
  Then the document contains all nested sections: kafkaContext, versions, outcome, hydration, retryInfo, and ttl = 15552000

Technical notes:
- `KafkaMessageContext` record: `MessageId` (string — from Kafka header), `PartyId` (string — from message body), `Topic` (string), `Partition` (int), `Offset` (long), `TopicRole` (string — "onboarding" | "amendment"), `ReceivedAt` (DateTimeOffset)
- `HydrationContext` record: `EntityId` (string), `MessageId` (string), `TopicRole` (string), `IncomingVersion` (int), `StoredVersion` (int), `Data` (EntityData), `WasApiFallback` (bool)
- `EntityData` record: property bag for hydration data; use `Dictionary<string, object> Properties { get; init; } = new()` or strongly-typed fields as the project evolves
- `EnrichmentResult` record: `StepName` (string), `Applied` (bool), `Duration` (TimeSpan — defaults to `TimeSpan.Zero`), `Data` (EntityData?)
- `AuditRecord` record with nested records: `KafkaContextInfo` (topic, partition, offset, receivedAt), `VersionInfo` (stored, incoming, gap, wasApiFallback), `HydrationInfo` (stepsApplied, stepsSkipped, totalDurationMs, stepBreakdown list), `RetryInfo` (attemptNumber, wasRetry, deadLettered), `Ttl` (int = 15552000)
- `AuditRecord.ProcessedDate` is a string in YYYY-MM-DD format — used as Cosmos partition key for audit-metrics
- `AuditRecord` has a `ToCosmosDocument()` method that returns a JSON-serialisable object matching the Cosmos document schema in the architecture document
- `AmendmentMessage`, `AmendPayload`, `Operation` records as defined in architecture: `Operation` carries `OperationType` (string), `Parameters` (Dictionary<string, object>), `OperationDetails` (Dictionary<string, object>)

EPIC: Infrastructure
STORY-3: Custom exception hierarchy

As the system
I want a typed exception hierarchy where every domain exception carries EntityId and MessageId
So that all failure log entries are structured and queryable by entity and message identity

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a MessageValidationException is thrown
  When it is caught as a FunctionAppException
  Then EntityId and MessageId are accessible on the base class
- Given a BusinessRuleViolationException is thrown
  When it is inspected
  Then RuleName is accessible alongside EntityId and MessageId
- Given an EnrichmentStepException is thrown
  When it is caught
  Then StepName is accessible alongside EntityId and MessageId
- Given any FunctionAppException is created with an inner exception
  When InnerException is accessed
  Then the original exception is retained

Technical notes:
- `FunctionAppException` is `abstract` extending `Exception`; constructor: `(string message, string entityId, string messageId, Exception inner = null)`; exposes `EntityId` and `MessageId` properties
- `MessageValidationException : FunctionAppException` — thrown on deserialization failure or missing required Kafka header; ErrorCategory = Permanent
- `BusinessRuleViolationException : FunctionAppException` — carries `RuleName` (string); thrown by amendment validator for rule violations; ErrorCategory = Permanent
- `EnrichmentStepException : FunctionAppException` — carries `StepName` (string); thrown by hydration steps on transient failure; ErrorCategory = Transient
- Use `sealed` on all three concrete exception types
- All constructors follow the same `(string message, string entityId, string messageId, Exception inner = null)` pattern from the base class

EPIC: Infrastructure
STORY-4: Error classification

As the system
I want an IErrorClassifier that maps any exception to ErrorCategory.Transient, Permanent, or Unknown
So that the batch error handler can route each failed message to retry or dead-letter without embedded switch logic

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a CosmosException with StatusCode 429 (TooManyRequests)
  When ErrorClassifier.Classify is called
  Then ErrorCategory.Transient is returned
- Given a CosmosException with StatusCode 412 (PreconditionFailed)
  When ErrorClassifier.Classify is called
  Then ErrorCategory.Transient is returned
- Given a JsonException
  When ErrorClassifier.Classify is called
  Then ErrorCategory.Permanent is returned
- Given a MessageValidationException
  When ErrorClassifier.Classify is called
  Then ErrorCategory.Permanent is returned
- Given a BusinessRuleViolationException
  When ErrorClassifier.Classify is called
  Then ErrorCategory.Permanent is returned
- Given a TaskCanceledException
  When ErrorClassifier.Classify is called
  Then ErrorCategory.Transient is returned
- Given an exception type not listed in any classification rule
  When ErrorClassifier.Classify is called
  Then ErrorCategory.Unknown is returned

Technical notes:
- `ErrorCategory` enum: `Transient`, `Permanent`, `Unknown`
- `IErrorClassifier` interface: `ErrorCategory Classify(Exception ex)`
- `ErrorClassifier : IErrorClassifier` (sealed) uses C# switch expression with pattern matching
- `HttpRequestException` with `StatusCode` in `{ ServiceUnavailable, GatewayTimeout, TooManyRequests }` → Transient
- `CosmosException` with `TooManyRequests` → Transient; `PreconditionFailed` → Transient; `BadRequest` → Permanent
- `TaskCanceledException`, `TimeoutException`, `OperationCanceledException` → Transient
- `JsonException`, `MessageValidationException`, `BusinessRuleViolationException`, `CosmosException(BadRequest)` → Permanent
- Default (`_`) → `ErrorCategory.Unknown` — treated as Transient by the batch handler (conservative)
- Register as singleton: `services.AddSingleton<IErrorClassifier, ErrorClassifier>()`

EPIC: Infrastructure
STORY-5: Shared service interfaces, DI extension, and ValidationResult

As a developer
I want all cross-cutting service interfaces and a shared DI extension method defined
So that function apps register dependencies from a single call and all contracts are discoverable in one place

Acceptance criteria:
- Given the DI container is built with AddSharedServices()
  When IEnrichmentStep implementations are resolved
  Then IEnumerable<IEnrichmentStep> returns all registered steps
- Given the DI container is built with AddSharedServices()
  When IOperationHandler implementations are resolved
  Then IEnumerable<IOperationHandler> returns all registered handlers
- Given ValidationResult is created with IsRejected = true
  When the orchestrator inspects it
  Then Reason is accessible and IsNoOp is false
- Given IErrorClassifier is resolved from the container
  When Classify is called
  Then the registered ErrorClassifier implementation is returned

Technical notes:
- `IEnrichmentStep`: `bool AppliesTo(HydrationContext context)` and `Task<EnrichmentResult> EnrichAsync(HydrationContext context)`
- `IOperationHandler`: `string OperationType { get; }`, `ValidationResult Validate(Operation operation, EnrichedCustomer storedEntity)`, `EnrichedCustomer Apply(Operation operation, EnrichedCustomer storedEntity)`
- `IAuditService`: `Task FlushAsync(AuditRecord record)`
- `IRetryService`: `Task EnqueueAsync(KafkaMessageContext context, string originalPayload, int attemptCount)`
- `IDeadLetterService`: `Task SendAsync(KafkaMessageContext context, string originalPayload, string reason, int attempt)`
- `IHydrationPipeline`: `Task<IEnumerable<EnrichmentResult>> ExecuteAsync(HydrationContext context)`
- `IOutputAssembler`: `EnrichedCustomer Assemble(HydrationContext context, IEnumerable<EnrichmentResult> results)`
- `IIdempotencyService`: `Task<bool> IsDuplicateAsync(string messageId)` and `Task MarkProcessedAsync(string messageId)`
- `IAmendmentOrchestrator`: `Task<AmendmentResult> OrchestrateAsync(AmendmentMessage message, KafkaMessageContext context)`
- `IVersionGapDetector`: `Task<EntityData> ResolveDataAsync(int incomingVersion, int storedVersion, string entityId, EntityData messagePayloadData)`
- `IEntityApiClient`: `Task<EntityData> GetEntityAtVersionAsync(string entityId, int version)`
- `ValidationResult` record: `IsRejected` (bool), `IsNoOp` (bool), `Reason` (string?)
- `AmendmentResult` record: `IsNoOp` (bool), `Entity` (EnrichedCustomer?)
- `ServiceCollectionExtensions` static class with `AddSharedServices(this IServiceCollection services)` — registers `IErrorClassifier` → `ErrorClassifier` (singleton)

EPIC: Infrastructure
STORY-6: Cosmos DB client and container DI registration

As a developer
I want the CosmosClient and all three containers registered in DI with correct retry and TLS configuration
So that services inject the right container without duplicating connection logic anywhere

Acceptance criteria:
- Given the application runs in the Development environment
  When the CosmosClient is created
  Then TLS certificate validation is bypassed using DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator
- Given the application runs in the Development environment
  When startup completes
  Then all three containers (enriched-records, audit-metrics, idempotency-records) exist in the configured database
- Given the application runs in a non-Development environment
  When the CosmosClient is created
  Then no TLS bypass is applied
- Given the CosmosClient is configured
  When Cosmos returns 429 throttling responses
  Then up to 5 retry attempts are made with a maximum of 10 seconds total wait (WithThrottlingRetryOptions)
- Given CreateContainerIfNotExistsAsync is called on startup in Development
  When the container already exists
  Then no error is thrown (the operation is idempotent)

Technical notes:
- `CosmosClientBuilder(connectionString).WithThrottlingRetryOptions(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10), maxRetryAttemptsOnThrottledRequests: 5).Build()`
- Development path wraps `HttpClient` with `HttpClientHandler { ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback = HttpClientHandler.DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator }`
- Container partition keys: `enriched-records` → `/partyId`, `audit-metrics` → `/processedDate`, `idempotency-records` → `/messageId`
- Register each `Container` with a named key or factory so services can inject the correct container (e.g., named registrations or wrapper types `EnrichedRecordsContainer`, `AuditMetricsContainer`, `IdempotencyContainer`)
- `CosmosDbConnection` and `CosmosDbName` read from `IConfiguration` — never hardcoded
- Extension method: `AddCosmosDb(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration, IHostEnvironment environment)`
- Dev init gated by `environment.IsDevelopment()` — never runs in Azure

EPIC: Onboarding
STORY-7: KafkaMessageContext population and log scope

As the onboarding function app
I want a KafkaMessageContext populated from the Kafka trigger event and a log scope opened at the entry point
So that every downstream log entry automatically carries full Kafka correlation context in customDimensions

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a Kafka message arrives with a messageId header and a body containing partyId
  When the function entry point processes the message
  Then a KafkaMessageContext is created with MessageId from header, PartyId from body, Topic, Partition, Offset, TopicRole = "onboarding", and ReceivedAt = UtcNow
- Given a KafkaMessageContext is populated
  When _logger.BeginScope is called with the context properties
  Then MessageId, PartyId, Topic, Partition, Offset, and TopicRole appear in customDimensions for every log call inside the scope
- Given a Kafka message is missing the messageId header
  When KafkaMessageContext creation is attempted
  Then a MessageValidationException is thrown before any pipeline logic runs

Technical notes:
- Context is built at the function entry point — before any pipeline code runs
- Log scope: `_logger.BeginScope(new Dictionary<string, object> { ["MessageId"] = ctx.MessageId, ["PartyId"] = ctx.PartyId, ["Topic"] = ctx.Topic, ["Partition"] = ctx.Partition, ["Offset"] = ctx.Offset, ["TopicRole"] = ctx.TopicRole })`
- `MessageId` comes from Kafka message headers — if absent, throw `new MessageValidationException("Missing messageId header", entityId: "unknown", messageId: "unknown")`
- `PartyId` comes from the deserialized message body — same value as the Kafka partition key
- `TopicRole` is hardcoded per function app: `"onboarding"` for onboarding-func
- `ReceivedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` captured at entry point
- `KafkaMessageContextBuilder` static helper class (or factory method) encapsulates extraction and validation logic

EPIC: Onboarding
STORY-8: Onboarding function app — Kafka trigger and hosting

As the onboarding function app
I want a Kafka-triggered Azure Function with batch processing configured on the .NET 8 isolated worker model
So that onboarding messages are consumed at high throughput with per-message failure isolation

Acceptance criteria:
- Given the onboarding function app starts
  When the Kafka trigger is configured
  Then it connects to KafkaBootstrapServers and listens on the topic from KafkaTopic configuration
- Given a batch of Kafka messages arrives
  When the function is invoked
  Then each message in the batch is processed independently — a failure on one message does not halt others
- Given an OutOfMemoryException is thrown during batch processing
  When it propagates to the batch handler
  Then it is NOT caught — it rethrows to let the Functions runtime restart
- Given batch processing completes
  When the batch loop exits
  Then a single BatchCompleted log entry is written with total, succeeded, transientFailures, and permanentFailures counts

Technical notes:
- Project: `Onboarding.Function` targeting .NET 8 isolated worker model
- Function class: `OnboardingKafkaFunction`; trigger attribute: `[KafkaTrigger("%KafkaTopic%", "%KafkaBootstrapServers%", ConsumerGroup = "onboarding-func", Protocol = BrokerProtocol.Plaintext)]`
- `Program.cs` registers: `AddSharedServices()`, `AddCosmosDb(configuration, environment)`, `AddOnboardingServices()`
- Batch loop: `foreach (var message in messages) { try { await _pipeline.ProcessAsync(message); succeeded++; } catch (OutOfMemoryException) { throw; } catch (Exception ex) { /* classify and route */ } }`
- Exception routing: `ErrorCategory.Permanent` → `IDeadLetterService.SendAsync(ctx, payload, ex.Message, attempt: 1)`; `Transient`/`Unknown` → `IRetryService.EnqueueAsync(ctx, payload, attemptCount: 1)`
- `host.json` includes App Insights sampling: `maxTelemetryItemsPerSecond: 20`, `excludedTypes: "Exception;Trace"`, `enableDependencyTracking: true`; log level `Information` for Function and default
- `MaxBatchSize` and `MinBatchSize` configured on the Kafka trigger (values from configuration — not hardcoded)

EPIC: Onboarding
STORY-9: Hydration pipeline — IEnrichmentStep registration and parallel execution

As the onboarding function app
I want enrichment steps executed in parallel via Task.WhenAll with step-selector logic via AppliesTo
So that per-message hydration latency is bounded by the slowest single step rather than the sum of all steps

Acceptance criteria:
- Given multiple IEnrichmentStep implementations are registered in DI
  When HydrationPipeline.ExecuteAsync is called with a HydrationContext
  Then only steps where AppliesTo returns true are passed to Task.WhenAll
- Given two applicable steps run concurrently
  When both complete
  Then the results contain one EnrichmentResult per step with Applied = true
- Given a step's AppliesTo returns false
  When ExecuteAsync returns
  Then that step's name appears in the results with Applied = false and Duration = TimeSpan.Zero
- Given a step throws an EnrichmentStepException
  When ExecuteAsync propagates it
  Then the exception bubbles up to the caller — not swallowed inside the pipeline

Technical notes:
- `HydrationPipeline` (sealed) implementing `IHydrationPipeline`; injects `IEnumerable<IEnrichmentStep>`
- Execution: `var applicable = _steps.Where(s => s.AppliesTo(context)); var results = await Task.WhenAll(applicable.Select(s => s.EnrichAsync(context)));`
- Skipped steps: `_steps.Where(s => !s.AppliesTo(context)).Select(s => new EnrichmentResult { StepName = s.StepName, Applied = false, Duration = TimeSpan.Zero })`
- Return value combines applied results and skipped results
- Concrete steps to register: `AddressEnrichmentStep`, `CreditCheckEnrichmentStep`, `ComplianceEnrichmentStep` — all implementing `IEnrichmentStep`
- Each step exposes a `string StepName` property (used in the skipped list)
- Registration: `services.AddScoped<IEnrichmentStep, AddressEnrichmentStep>()` (same pattern for all steps)
- `IHydrationPipeline` registered: `services.AddScoped<IHydrationPipeline, HydrationPipeline>()`
- Steps apply based on `context.TopicRole` or message data — `AddressEnrichmentStep.AppliesTo` returns true for all messages; concrete applicability rules are stubs at this stage

EPIC: Onboarding
STORY-10: Hydration pipeline — output assembler

As the onboarding function app
I want an OutputAssembler that merges all EnrichmentResults into a final EnrichedCustomer with a populated AuditSummary
So that document construction and audit population happen in exactly one place

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a HydrationContext and a list of EnrichmentResults
  When OutputAssembler.Assemble is called
  Then the returned EnrichedCustomer has Id = context.EntityId and PartyId = context.EntityId
- Given EnrichmentResults where some have Applied = false
  When Assemble is called
  Then only steps with Applied = true appear in AuditSummary.LastHydrationSteps
- Given context.WasApiFallback is true
  When Assemble returns
  Then the assembled document's AuditSummary.WasApiFallback is true
- Given multiple applied results each with non-zero Duration
  When Assemble calculates AuditSummary
  Then no single step duration is omitted from the sum

Technical notes:
- `OutputAssembler` (sealed) implementing `IOutputAssembler`
- Method: `EnrichedCustomer Assemble(HydrationContext context, IEnumerable<EnrichmentResult> results)`
- Sets: `Id = context.EntityId`, `PartyId = context.EntityId`, `Version = context.IncomingVersion`, `LastUpdatedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`, `LastUpdatedBy` = `"onboarding-app"` when `context.TopicRole == "onboarding"`, else `"amendment-app"`
- `AuditSummary`: `LastMessageId = context.MessageId`, `LastKafkaOffset = context.Offset`, `LastHydrationSteps = applied.Select(r => r.StepName).ToList()`, `WasApiFallback = context.WasApiFallback`, `ProcessedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`
- Private `MergeData` method merges all applied `EnrichmentResult.Data` values into the document's collection properties
- `IOutputAssembler` registered: `services.AddScoped<IOutputAssembler, OutputAssembler>()`

EPIC: Onboarding
STORY-11: Onboarding pipeline — blind upsert to enriched-records

As the onboarding function app
I want the assembled EnrichedCustomer written to the enriched-records container via blind upsert
So that each onboarding message is durably persisted and re-delivery is harmless

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a valid onboarding message is processed end-to-end
  When OnboardingCosmosWriter.WriteAsync is called
  Then UpsertItemAsync is called on enriched-records with the assembled EnrichedCustomer and partyId as partition key
- Given an entity already exists in enriched-records
  When an onboarding message for the same partyId is re-delivered
  Then UpsertItemAsync overwrites the existing document without error (no ETag check — blind upsert)
- Given UpsertItemAsync throws a CosmosException 429 after SDK retries are exhausted
  When the exception propagates
  Then it reaches the batch error handler as Transient (not caught inside the writer)
- Given a successful upsert
  When WriteAsync completes
  Then the pipeline calls IAuditService.FlushAsync with the correct AuditRecord for this message

Technical notes:
- `OnboardingCosmosWriter` (sealed) implementing `IOnboardingCosmosWriter`
- `IOnboardingCosmosWriter`: `Task WriteAsync(EnrichedCustomer entity)`
- `UpsertItemAsync(entity, new PartitionKey(entity.PartyId))` — no `ItemRequestOptions.IfMatchEtag`
- Container: `enriched-records`, partition key: `/partyId`
- No idempotency check — blind upsert is by design; re-delivery overwrites with identical data
- `OnboardingPipeline` (sealed) implementing `IOnboardingPipeline` orchestrates: build `HydrationContext` → call `IHydrationPipeline.ExecuteAsync` → call `IOutputAssembler.Assemble` → call `IOnboardingCosmosWriter.WriteAsync` → call `IAuditService.FlushAsync`
- `IOnboardingPipeline`: `Task ProcessAsync(KafkaMessage message)`
- Register both: `services.AddScoped<IOnboardingCosmosWriter, OnboardingCosmosWriter>()` and `services.AddScoped<IOnboardingPipeline, OnboardingPipeline>()`

Dependencies: STORY-9, STORY-10, STORY-6, STORY-7

EPIC: Amendment
STORY-12: Amendment idempotency check

As the amendment function app
I want each incoming message checked against idempotency-records before processing
So that re-delivered messages are detected and silently skipped without rolling back subsequent amendments

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a messageId that already exists in idempotency-records
  When IsDuplicateAsync is called
  Then true is returned and a DuplicateMessageSkipped Information log is emitted
- Given a messageId that does NOT exist in idempotency-records
  When IsDuplicateAsync is called
  Then false is returned and processing continues
- Given a message is successfully processed end-to-end
  When MarkProcessedAsync is called
  Then CreateItemAsync writes an IdempotencyRecord to idempotency-records with messageId as both id and partition key
- Given two concurrent executions for the same messageId both call CreateItemAsync
  When the second attempt receives a 409 Conflict CosmosException
  Then it is treated as success — the message was already handled — and does not rethrow

Technical notes:
- `IdempotencyService` (sealed) implementing `IIdempotencyService`
- `IsDuplicateAsync`: `ReadItemAsync<IdempotencyRecord>(messageId, new PartitionKey(messageId))` — succeeds → duplicate (return true); `CosmosException(NotFound)` → not a duplicate (return false)
- `MarkProcessedAsync`: `CreateItemAsync(record, new PartitionKey(messageId))` — catches `CosmosException` with `StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.Conflict` and returns without rethrowing
- `IdempotencyRecord` record: `Id` (= MessageId), `MessageId` (string), `ProcessedAt` (DateTimeOffset), `Ttl` (int = 604800 — 7 days in seconds)
- `MarkProcessedAsync` is called AFTER successful pipeline completion — not before
- Container: `idempotency-records`, partition key: `/messageId`
- ErrorCategory for Conflict suppression: no error — it is an expected race condition, not a failure
- Register: `services.AddScoped<IIdempotencyService, IdempotencyService>()`

Dependencies: STORY-2, STORY-6, STORY-5

EPIC: Amendment
STORY-13: Version gap detection and API fallback with caching

As the amendment function app
I want the incoming message version compared to the stored entity version, fetching from the external API when the gap is 2 or more
So that missing Kafka messages do not leave the entity in a stale or incorrect state

Acceptance criteria:
- Given incoming version = 5 and stored version = 4 (gap = 1)
  When ResolveDataAsync is called
  Then the message payload data is returned as-is — no API call is made
- Given incoming version = 6 and stored version = 4 (gap = 2)
  When ResolveDataAsync is called
  Then GetEntityAtVersionAsync is called on the external API and a VersionGapDetected warning is logged
- Given the same entityId and version are requested twice within 60 seconds
  When the second call would go to the API
  Then the cached EntityData is returned and no outbound HTTP call is made
- Given GetEntityAtVersionAsync succeeds
  When the HydrationContext is built
  Then WasApiFallback is set to true and TelemetryClient.TrackDependency records the API call

Technical notes:
- `VersionGapDetector` (sealed) implementing `IVersionGapDetector`
- Gap formula: `gap = incomingVersion - storedVersion`; gap >= 2 → API fallback; gap < 2 → use message payload
- Cache key: `$"api-entity-{entityId}-v{version}"` using `IMemoryCache`; absolute expiry of 60 seconds
- Warning log: `_logger.LogWarning("VersionGapDetected {EntityId} stored={StoredVersion} incoming={IncomingVersion} gap={Gap}", context.EntityId, context.StoredVersion, context.IncomingVersion, gap)`
- `EntityApiClient` (sealed) implementing `IEntityApiClient`; typed `HttpClient` registered with Polly standard resilience: `MaxRetryAttempts = 3`, `Delay = 200ms`, `BackoffType = Exponential`, circuit breaker `FailureRatio = 0.5, MinimumThroughput = 10, SamplingDuration = 30s`, `Timeout = 5s`
- `TelemetryClient.TrackDependency(new DependencyTelemetry { Name = "EntityApi.GetEntityAtVersion", Target = _apiBaseUrl, Data = $"GET /entities/{entityId}/versions/{version}", Duration = timer.Elapsed, Success = success, Timestamp = startTime })`
- Register: `services.AddMemoryCache()`, `services.AddScoped<IVersionGapDetector, VersionGapDetector>()`, `services.AddHttpClient<IEntityApiClient, EntityApiClient>().AddStandardResilienceHandler(...)`
- `ApiBaseUrl` read from `IConfiguration` — never hardcoded

EPIC: Amendment
STORY-14: Amendment function app — Kafka trigger and hosting

As the amendment function app
I want a Kafka-triggered Azure Function with idempotency-first entry point and batch processing
So that amendment messages are consumed efficiently with duplicate detection before any business logic runs

Acceptance criteria:
- Given the amendment function app starts
  When the Kafka trigger is configured
  Then it connects to KafkaBootstrapServers and listens on the amendment topic with ConsumerGroup = "amendment-func"
- Given a batch of amendment messages arrives
  When each message is processed
  Then IIdempotencyService.IsDuplicateAsync is called first — if true, processing halts for that message
- Given a message passes the idempotency check
  When the amendment pipeline runs
  Then TopicRole in the KafkaMessageContext is "amendment"
- Given an OutOfMemoryException is thrown
  When the batch handler encounters it
  Then it is rethrown immediately — not routed to retry or dead-letter

Technical notes:
- Project: `Amendment.Function` targeting .NET 8 isolated worker model
- Function class: `AmendmentKafkaFunction`; trigger attribute with `ConsumerGroup = "amendment-func"` and amendment topic
- Entry point sequence: (1) build `KafkaMessageContext` with `TopicRole = "amendment"`, (2) `IsDuplicateAsync` — if true log and return, (3) call amendment pipeline, (4) on success call `MarkProcessedAsync`
- `Program.cs` registers: `AddSharedServices()`, `AddCosmosDb(configuration, environment)`, `AddAmendmentServices()`
- `AddAmendmentServices()` registers: `IIdempotencyService`, `IVersionGapDetector`, `IEntityApiClient`, `IOperationHandler` implementations, `IAmendmentOrchestrator`, `IRetryService`, `IDeadLetterService`, `IAuditService`, `ServiceBusClient`

EPIC: Amendment
STORY-15: Amendment conditional logic — operation handlers

As the amendment function app
I want per-operation-type handlers (add, remove, update) that each implement IOperationHandler
So that each operation type's apply logic is isolated and new types can be added without touching existing handlers

Acceptance criteria:
- Given an AddOperationHandler and an operation with OperationType = "add"
  When Apply is called with a stored entity that does not already contain the target item
  Then the new item is appended to the correct collection with AddedAt = UtcNow and AddedBy = "amendment-app"
- Given a RemoveOperationHandler and an operation with OperationType = "remove"
  When Apply is called
  Then the item matching the stable ID in parameters is removed from the collection
- Given an UpdateOperationHandler and an operation with OperationType = "update"
  When Apply is called
  Then only fields specified in operationDetails are updated on the matching item — other fields are unchanged
- Given the orchestrator resolves a handler by OperationType = "add"
  When a single handler is expected
  Then only AddOperationHandler is returned (no ambiguity)

Technical notes:
- `AddOperationHandler` (sealed): `OperationType = "add"` — appends new item; `AddedBy = "amendment-app"`, `AddedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`
- `RemoveOperationHandler` (sealed): `OperationType = "remove"` — removes item matched by stable ID from `parameters` (`addressId`, `phoneId`, `emailId`, `operationId`)
- `UpdateOperationHandler` (sealed): `OperationType = "update"` — patches matching item with fields from `operationDetails`; matched by stable ID in `parameters`
- `Validate` method stubs return `ValidationResult { IsRejected = false, IsNoOp = false }` at this story — full validation rules are in STORY-16
- Target collection determined by which stable ID key is present in `parameters`/`operationDetails`
- Register all three as `IOperationHandler`: `services.AddScoped<IOperationHandler, AddOperationHandler>()` (same pattern for all)

EPIC: Amendment
STORY-16: Amendment conditional logic — validator

As the amendment function app
I want the Validate method on each IOperationHandler to enforce business rules before any operations are applied
So that malformed or rule-violating messages are dead-lettered immediately without any partial state change

Acceptance criteria:
- Given an "add" operation where the target item already exists in the stored entity
  When Validate is called on AddOperationHandler
  Then ValidationResult.IsRejected = true and Reason = "DuplicateRecord"
- Given a "remove" operation where no matching item exists in the stored entity
  When Validate is called on RemoveOperationHandler
  Then ValidationResult.IsRejected = true and Reason = "RecordNotFound"
- Given an "update" operation where operationDetails is identical to the current record
  When Validate is called on UpdateOperationHandler
  Then ValidationResult.IsNoOp = true (skip silently — not an error)
- Given an "update" operation where the target item does not exist
  When Validate is called
  Then ValidationResult.IsRejected = true and Reason = "RecordNotFound"
- Given an "add" operation that sets isPreferred = true when another item in the same collection already has isPreferred = true
  When Validate is called
  Then ValidationResult.IsRejected = true and Reason = "IsPreferredConflict"
- Given an OperationType that has no registered IOperationHandler
  When the orchestrator attempts to resolve a handler
  Then a BusinessRuleViolationException is thrown with RuleName = "UnknownOperationType"

Technical notes:
- Validation logic lives in the `Validate` method of each handler — not in a separate class
- Matching uses the same stable ID lookup as Apply: `addressId`, `phoneId`, `emailId`, `operationId` from `parameters`
- `BusinessRuleViolationException` is thrown by the orchestrator (not by Validate) when OperationType is unrecognised
- `IsPreferredConflict` check: if `add`/`update` sets `isPreferred: true` AND another item in the same collection already has `IsPreferred = true`, reject — the caller must explicitly clear the existing preferred item first
- ErrorCategory for `BusinessRuleViolationException` = Permanent (from STORY-4) — dead-letter immediately, no retry

Dependencies: STORY-3, STORY-5, STORY-15

EPIC: Amendment
STORY-17: Amendment conditional logic — orchestrator and ETag-gated upsert

As the amendment function app
I want a two-pass orchestrator that validates all operations before applying any, then writes the result with ETag gating
So that amendment messages succeed atomically or are dead-lettered without leaving partial state in Cosmos

Acceptance criteria:
- Given an amendment message where one of multiple operations fails validation
  When the orchestrator runs pass 1
  Then a BusinessRuleViolationException is thrown and NO operations are applied to the stored entity
- Given all operations pass validation and at least one is not a no-op
  When the orchestrator runs pass 2 and pass 3
  Then all non-no-op operations are applied sequentially and UpsertItemAsync is called with the ETag from the original ReadItemAsync
- Given all operations are no-ops
  When the orchestrator completes
  Then AmendmentResult.IsNoOp = true is returned and no Cosmos write occurs
- Given UpsertItemAsync receives a 412 PreconditionFailed (ETag conflict)
  When the exception propagates
  Then it is classified as Transient and the message is enqueued to the retry queue immediately (no 30s delay)
- Given ReadItemAsync returns NotFound (onboarding document not yet written)
  When the exception is caught
  Then the message is enqueued to the retry queue with ScheduledEnqueueTime 30 seconds in the future

Technical notes:
- `AmendmentOrchestrator` (sealed) implementing `IAmendmentOrchestrator`
- Pass 1: `foreach` all operations — call `handler.Validate(op, storedEntity)`, accumulate `violations` and `noOps`; if `violations.Any()` throw `BusinessRuleViolationException`
- Pass 2: apply non-no-op operations sequentially: `foreach (var op in ops.Where((_, i) => !noOps.Contains(i))) updatedEntity = handler.Apply(op, updatedEntity)`
- Pass 3: `UpsertItemAsync(updatedEntity, new PartitionKey(entityId), new ItemRequestOptions { IfMatchEtag = response.ETag })`
- "NotFound" during read → `IRetryService.EnqueueAsync` with 30-second scheduled delay (not rethrown as Transient — handled explicitly)
- ETag 412 → propagates as `CosmosException(PreconditionFailed)` → classified as Transient by batch handler → retry queue (no delay)
- After successful upsert: `IIdempotencyService.MarkProcessedAsync(messageId)` then `IAuditService.FlushAsync(auditRecord)`
- Register: `services.AddScoped<IAmendmentOrchestrator, AmendmentOrchestrator>()`
- Container: `enriched-records`, partition key: `/partyId`

EPIC: Amendment
STORY-18: Dead-letter and retry flow — Service Bus integration

As the amendment function app
I want RetryService and DeadLetterService that enqueue messages to Service Bus with full Kafka context preserved
So that failed messages are durably held with enough context for retry or human review

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a transient failure and attemptCount < 3
  When RetryService.EnqueueAsync is called
  Then a ServiceBusMessage is sent to the {topicRole}-retry queue with ScheduledEnqueueTime 30 seconds ahead and ApplicationProperties["attemptCount"] incremented by 1
- Given a message that has exhausted 3 retry attempts
  When DeadLetterService.SendAsync is called
  Then the message is sent to the {topicRole}-deadletter queue and a MessageDeadLettered Error log is emitted
- Given any Service Bus message is constructed for retry or dead-letter
  When the message properties are inspected
  Then messageId, partyId, topic, partition, offset, and topicRole are all present in ApplicationProperties
- Given a permanent failure (ErrorCategory.Permanent) occurs in the batch handler
  When the message is routed
  Then DeadLetterService.SendAsync is called with attempt = 1 (dead-letter immediately — no retry)
- Given an ETag conflict (PreconditionFailed)
  When it reaches the retry service
  Then ScheduledEnqueueTime is DateTimeOffset.UtcNow (no delay — immediate retry, unlike the 30s delay used for NotFound)

Technical notes:
- `RetryService` (sealed) implementing `IRetryService`; `DeadLetterService` (sealed) implementing `IDeadLetterService`
- Both inject `ServiceBusClient` (singleton) and `ILogger`
- Queue name pattern: `{context.TopicRole}-retry` and `{context.TopicRole}-deadletter`
- `attemptCount` carried in `ApplicationProperties["attemptCount"]` — NOT using Service Bus built-in `DeliveryCount`
- Max attempts = 3: when `attemptCount + 1 > 3`, route to dead-letter instead of retry
- ETag conflict uses `ScheduledEnqueueTime = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`; NotFound and other transient failures use `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddSeconds(30)`
- Dead-letter log: `_logger.LogError("MessageDeadLettered {MessageId} {EntityId} {Reason} attempt={Attempt}", ...)`
- `ServiceBusConnection` read from `IConfiguration`; `ServiceBusClient` registered as singleton
- Register: `services.AddSingleton(sp => new ServiceBusClient(sp.GetRequiredService<IConfiguration>()["ServiceBusConnection"]))`, `services.AddScoped<IRetryService, RetryService>()`, `services.AddScoped<IDeadLetterService, DeadLetterService>()`

EPIC: Observability
STORY-19: Batch error handling

As the system
I want the batch processing loop to catch exceptions per message, classify them, and route without halting other messages
So that a single bad message does not prevent the rest of the batch from being processed

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a batch of 5 messages where message 3 throws a JsonException
  When the batch loop completes
  Then messages 1, 2, 4, and 5 are processed successfully and message 3 is sent to dead-letter
- Given a message throws a Transient exception
  When the batch handler catches it
  Then the message is enqueued to the retry queue (not dead-lettered)
- Given a message throws ErrorCategory.Unknown
  When the batch handler handles it
  Then it is treated as Transient — enqueued to retry queue
- Given an OutOfMemoryException is thrown inside the batch loop
  When it propagates to the catch block
  Then it is rethrown immediately — not caught or routed
- Given a batch finishes with mixed outcomes
  When the loop exits
  Then exactly one BatchCompleted log entry is written with accurate total, succeeded, transientFailures, and permanentFailures counts

Technical notes:
- Batch loop lives in both `OnboardingKafkaFunction` and `AmendmentKafkaFunction` function entry points
- Per-message catch: `catch (Exception ex)` with `catch (OutOfMemoryException) { throw; }` before the general catch (or re-throw inside)
- Routing: `ErrorCategory.Permanent` → `_deadLetterService.SendAsync(ctx, payload, ex.Message, attempt: 1)`; `Transient`/`Unknown` → `_retryService.EnqueueAsync(ctx, payload, attemptCount: 1)`
- Error log per failed message: `_logger.LogError(ex, "MessageProcessingFailed {MessageId} {EntityId} {Category} {ExceptionType}", messageId, entityId, category, ex.GetType().Name)`
- Counters: `int total = 0, succeeded = 0, transientFailures = 0, permanentFailures = 0` accumulated in the loop
- Batch summary after loop: `_logger.LogWarning("BatchCompleted total={Total} succeeded={Succeeded} transientFailures={Transient} permanentFailures={Permanent}", total, succeeded, transientFailures, permanentFailures)`
- No component below the function entry point catches and swallows exceptions — only the top-level batch handler decides routing

EPIC: Observability
STORY-20: Audit service — ILogger structured logging

As the system
I want AuditService and pipeline components to emit structured ILogger log entries for all significant events
So that Application Insights receives queryable, structured telemetry for dashboards, alerts, and debugging without custom event ingestion cost

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a message is processed successfully
  When AuditService.FlushAsync is called
  Then a MessageProcessed Information log is emitted with MessageId, EntityId, TopicRole, StepsApplied, WasApiFallback, and TotalDurationMs as structured properties
- Given a version gap >= 2 is detected
  When VersionGapDetector.ResolveDataAsync runs
  Then a VersionGapDetected Warning log is emitted with EntityId, StoredVersion, IncomingVersion, and Gap
- Given a duplicate message is detected
  When IdempotencyService.IsDuplicateAsync returns true
  Then a DuplicateMessageSkipped Information log is emitted with MessageId, EntityId, and TopicRole
- Given a message is sent to dead-letter
  When DeadLetterService.SendAsync is called
  Then a MessageDeadLettered Error log is emitted with MessageId, EntityId, Reason, and attempt number

Technical notes:
- `ILogger<T>` structured logging only — no `Console.Write`, no string interpolation in log templates
- Exact log message templates from architecture: `"MessageProcessed {MessageId} {EntityId} {TopicRole} {StepsApplied} {WasApiFallback} {TotalDurationMs}ms"`, `"VersionGapDetected {EntityId} stored={StoredVersion} incoming={IncomingVersion} gap={Gap}"`, `"DuplicateMessageSkipped {MessageId} {EntityId} {TopicRole}"`, `"MessageDeadLettered {MessageId} {EntityId} {Reason} attempt={Attempt}"`
- Log scope (from STORY-7) ensures all log entries within the message processing scope carry Kafka context in customDimensions automatically
- `TelemetryClient` is used in `AuditService` ONLY for dependency tracking (external API calls via `TrackDependency`) — not for custom events or metrics
- `host.json` sampling configuration: adaptive sampling enabled, `maxTelemetryItemsPerSecond: 20`, `excludedTypes: "Exception;Trace"` (exceptions and traces always fully captured)

EPIC: Observability
STORY-21: Audit service — Cosmos flush

As the system
I want AuditService.FlushAsync to write a structured audit document to the audit-metrics Cosmos container
So that business stakeholders and compliance teams have a queryable, TTL-managed audit trail for every processing event

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a successfully processed message
  When AuditService.FlushAsync is called with an AuditRecord
  Then CreateItemAsync is called on the audit-metrics container with the mapped Cosmos document
- Given an AuditRecord is written to Cosmos
  When the document is stored
  Then the Cosmos document id = messageId, partition key = processedDate (YYYY-MM-DD), and ttl = 15552000
- Given the AuditRecord has hydration step results
  When ToCosmosDocument maps the record
  Then stepsApplied, stepsSkipped, totalDurationMs, and stepBreakdown are all present in the nested hydration object
- Given CreateItemAsync returns a 409 Conflict (same messageId flushed twice)
  When the exception is caught inside FlushAsync
  Then it is logged as Warning and not rethrown (duplicate audit write is not a pipeline failure)

Technical notes:
- `AuditService` (sealed) implementing `IAuditService`
- Constructor injects: `ILogger<AuditService>`, `TelemetryClient`, and the `audit-metrics` Cosmos `Container`
- `FlushAsync` calls: (1) `_logger.LogInformation("MessageProcessed ...")` then (2) `_auditContainer.CreateItemAsync(record.ToCosmosDocument(), new PartitionKey(record.ProcessedDate))`
- `AuditRecord.ToCosmosDocument()` returns an anonymous object or dedicated Cosmos document class matching the full schema: nested `kafkaContext`, `versions`, `outcome`, `hydration` (with `stepBreakdown`), `retryInfo`, `ttl = 15552000`
- Container: `audit-metrics`, partition key: `/processedDate`
- `ttl` field = 15552000 (180 days in seconds) set per-document — enables per-record retention extension for compliance disputes
- Register: `services.AddScoped<IAuditService, AuditService>()`

EPIC: Operations
STORY-22: DLQ admin tool — API

As an operator
I want a standalone C# minimal API with three endpoints to list, requeue, and discard dead-letter queue messages
So that I can action parked messages without needing direct Service Bus tooling

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a GET request to /api/dlq/{queueName}
  When the dead-letter queue contains messages
  Then up to 50 messages are returned as JSON with MessageId, PartyId, Topic, Partition, Offset, Reason, Attempts, DeadLetteredAt, and Body — without consuming them from the queue
- Given a POST request to /api/dlq/{queueName}/requeue/{messageId}
  When the message is found in the dead-letter queue
  Then it is moved to the corresponding retry queue with attemptCount reset to 0 and a 200 OK is returned
- Given a POST or DELETE request where the messageId is not in the queue
  When the action is attempted
  Then a 404 Not Found is returned
- Given a DELETE request to /api/dlq/{queueName}/{messageId}
  When the message is found
  Then it is permanently removed from the dead-letter queue and 200 OK is returned
- Given a GET request to list messages
  When PeekMessagesAsync is called
  Then no messages are consumed (peek-only — non-destructive)

Technical notes:
- Project: `DlqAdmin` — `WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args)` minimal API
- `ServiceBusClient` registered as singleton from `IConfiguration["ServiceBusConnection"]`
- GET: `CreateReceiver(queueName, new ServiceBusReceiverOptions { SubQueue = SubQueue.DeadLetter, ReceiveMode = ServiceBusReceiveMode.PeekLock })` + `PeekMessagesAsync(maxMessages: 50)`
- POST (requeue): receive (ReceiveMessagesAsync), find by MessageId, create new `ServiceBusMessage` with `attemptCount = 0`, send to `queueName.Replace("-deadletter", "-retry")`, then `CompleteMessageAsync`
- DELETE (discard): receive, find by MessageId, call `CompleteMessageAsync` to remove from queue permanently
- `app.UseStaticFiles()` serves the HTML frontend from `wwwroot/`
- Queue names accepted: `amendment-deadletter`, `onboarding-deadletter`
- `ServiceBusConnection` from `appsettings.Development.json` pointing to local Service Bus emulator

EPIC: Infrastructure
STORY-25: CI/CD pipeline — GitHub Actions workflows

As a developer
I want ci.yml and pr-checks.yml GitHub Actions workflows with branch protection rules on main
So that every PR is gate-checked and every merge to main produces a versioned, traceable build artifact

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a pull request is opened against main
  When pr-checks.yml runs
  Then `dotnet restore`, `dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore`, and `dotnet test --no-build` all pass as PR gates before the PR can merge
- Given a push to main occurs
  When ci.yml runs
  Then the build produces an artifact named `function-app-{github.sha}` with 7-day retention
- Given `dotnet test` runs in ci.yml
  When it completes
  Then XPlat Code Coverage results are uploaded as a `coverage-report` artifact
- Given branch protection is configured on main
  When a developer attempts a direct push to main
  Then the push is rejected (PR required) and `PR Checks / Build and Test` status check must pass before merge
- Given the deploy job stub exists as a comment in ci.yml
  When Azure access becomes available
  Then the job can be uncommented without workflow redesign

Technical notes:
- `ci.yml`: triggers on `push: branches: [main]` and `workflow_dispatch`; env `DOTNET_VERSION: 8.x`, `BUILD_CONFIGURATION: Release`
- Steps: Checkout → Setup .NET → Restore → Build (`--no-restore`) → Test (`tests/**/*.Tests.csproj --no-build --collect "XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory ./coverage`) → Upload coverage (`actions/upload-artifact@v4`, name: `coverage-report`) → Publish (`src/**/*.csproj --output ./publish`) → Upload artifact (`function-app-${{ github.sha }}`, `retention-days: 7`)
- `pr-checks.yml`: triggers on `pull_request: branches: [main]`; same steps except no Publish and no artifact upload
- Stub deploy job commented out targeting `onboarding-func-dev` with `Azure/functions-action@v1` and `AZURE_FUNCTIONAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE` secret
- Branch protection: require PR, require status check `PR Checks / Build and Test`, require branches up to date before merge
